source.title: Some open problems of graph theory.

accepted.question_text: Determine the minimum possible value of the largest element x_n among all strictly increasing n-term sequences 0 ≤ x_1 < x_2 < ⋯ < x_n of nonnegative integers for which every difference x_j - x_i with 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n is distinct.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. (G. Burosch and J.-M. Laborde) On the minimum value \(\rho\) (n) of \(x_ n\), where \(0\leq x_ 1<x_ 2<...<x_ n\) is a set of non- negative integers with all differences distinct.

accepted.question_text: Given a finite set of integers, decide whether there exists a bipartite graph whose list of vertex degrees is exactly that set of integers.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. (R. I. Tyshkevich) On recognizing whether for a set of integers there exists a bipartite graph for which that set is the list of vertex-degrees.

accepted.question_text: Determine all 2-connected r-regular graphs for which there is a Hamiltonian circuit or a cycle of length 2r + 4.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. (H.-J. Voss) On determining all 2-connected r-regular graphs for which the length of a Hamiltonian circuit or a cycle is equal to \(2r+4.\)

accepted.question_text: Find the smallest integer k such that every k-Hamiltonian graph is Hamiltonian connected.

evidence.quote: Problem 10. (Z. Skupień) On finding the smallest k such that each k- Hamiltonian graph is Hamiltonian connected.

trace.notes: Used the zbMATH HTML record itself as the primary source because its visible summary paragraph contains the numbered problem statements directly.
Extracted ten numbered candidate problems from the single summary paragraph on the source page.
Rewrote the distinct-difference integer-set problem into a standalone minimization question while preserving the source constraints.
Rewrote the bipartite degree-set recognition problem into direct decision-question form.
Kept the source wording close to the original because the problem statement is short but still technically usable.
Rewrote the k-Hamiltonian threshold problem into a direct extremal formulation.
Moved to needs_review because the specific conditions on chromatic number, edge count, and triangle count are not stated in the source snippet.
Moved to needs_review because the statement only names a topic and does not provide a concrete open question.
Moved to needs_review because the phrase 'containing a non-Hamiltonian graph' is too compressed to determine the intended formal problem without adding unsupported interpretation.
Moved to needs_review because the source snippet does not specify the maximal-clique problem or the conjectured algorithmic claim precisely enough.
Moved to needs_review because ICE is expanded but the technical objects are not defined well enough in the source snippet to make a standalone question without importing outside facts.
Moved to needs_review because the term 'general bridge graphs' is not defined in the source snippet.
